message.content:
I don’t have a way to directly measure your connection from here, but I can guide you through a quick test on your own machine.

---

## 1. Using a Web Browser (easiest)

1. Open a browser and go to a speed‑test site such as:
   * https://www.speedtest.net/
   * https://fast.com/
2. Click “Go” or “Start” and wait for the test to finish.  
   The page will display your **download** and **upload** speeds in Mbps.

---

## 2. Using the Command Line (Windows)

If you prefer a terminal‑based test, you can use PowerShell to download a known file and time it. Here’s a quick example:

```powershell
$start = Get-Date
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin" -OutFile "$env:TEMP\speedtest.bin"
$end = Get-Date
$duration = ($end - $start).TotalSeconds
$bytes = (Get-Item "$env:TEMP\speedtest.bin").Length
$mbps = ($bytes / 1MB) / $duration
Write-Host "Download speed: $([math]::Round($mbps,2)) Mbps"
```

**What it does:**
- Downloads a 100 MB file from Hetzner’s public speed‑test server.
- Measures the time taken.
- Calculates the speed in megabits per second (Mbps).

> **Tip:** Delete the downloaded file afterward:
> ```powershell
> Remove-Item "$env:TEMP\speedtest.bin"
> ```

---

## 3. Using the Command Line (Linux/macOS)

```bash
# Download a 100 MB file and time it
time curl -o /tmp/speedtest.bin https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin
# Calculate Mbps
bytes=$(stat -c%s /tmp/speedtest.bin)
seconds=$(cat /tmp/speedtest.time | grep real | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d 's')
mbps=$(echo "scale=2; ($bytes/1048576)/$seconds" | bc)
echo "Download speed: $mbps Mbps"
# Clean up
rm /tmp/speedtest.bin
```

---

## 4. Using a Dedicated Tool

If you want more detailed results (latency, jitter, packet loss, etc.), consider installing a dedicated speed‑test client:

| OS | Install Command |
|----|-----------------|
| Windows | `choco install speedtest-cli` |
| macOS | `brew install speedtest-cli` |
| Linux | `sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli` (Debian/Ubuntu) |

Then run:

```bash
speedtest
```

---

### Quick Summary

| Method | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| Browser speed‑test | Very easy, no setup | Requires a GUI |
| PowerShell script | Works on Windows, no extra software | Requires PowerShell |
| Curl script | Works on Linux/macOS, no extra software | Requires shell scripting |
| Dedicated CLI tool | Detailed metrics | Needs installation |

Pick the method that best fits your environment. If you run into any issues or need help interpreting the results, just let me know!
